title: Sampling for Flow Cytometry (FCM)
author: Sarah Giuliani
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.f25bqg6

steps.title: Prepare sample cryovials
steps.instruction: Aliquot 900 µl of seawater (artificial seawater salts or complete sterile medium) into labeled 1.2 ml cryovials. If samples are not seawater-based, use an appropriate diluent of the same ionic strength (e.g., sterile medium, sterile freshwater salts).

substeps.instruction: Adjust dilution if necessary (this protocol uses a 10-fold dilution; dilute more for very concentrated or sample-limited cases, or dilute less/not at all if sample is <1E6 cells/ml).

steps.title: Collect samples
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl of sample into the cryovial containing 900 µl of seawater, ensuring the cryovial cap remains clean and sterile.

steps.title: Fix samples with glutaraldehyde
steps.instruction: Fix the samples in a chemical fume hood to a final glutaraldehyde concentration of 0.125%.

substeps.instruction: Lay out cryovial caps with the inside facing up.
Use a repeater pipet to add 5 µl of 25% glutaraldehyde to each cap.
Cap each tube and mix well by inverting several times.
Incubate for 10 minutes in the dark.

steps.title: Freeze and store samples
steps.instruction: Flash-freeze the tubes in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C until analysis.
